1	# @pantoken/plugin-logos
2	
3	Instructure product logos as SVGs, data URIs, and image tokens. Covers Canvas, Mastery, Parchment,
4	Instructure, LearnPlatform, and Ignite AI, in the standard layouts (horizontal, stacked, icon) and
5	color modes (full-color, color, dark, reversed, and more). The SVGs ship in the package.
6	
7	## Install
8	
9	```sh
10	npm i @pantoken/plugin-logos
11	```
12	
13	Also available as `pantoken/logos`.
14	
15	## Usage
16	
17	Get a logo in code:
18	
19	```ts
20	import { getLogoSvg, getLogoDataUri } from "@pantoken/plugin-logos";
21	
22	const svg = getLogoSvg("canvas", "horizontal", "full-color");
23	const uri = getLogoDataUri("mastery", "icon", "color");
24	```
25	
26	Or use the image tokens in CSS:
27	
28	```ts
29	import "@pantoken/plugin-logos/logos.css";
30	```
31	
32	```css
33	.brand {
34	  background-image: var(--instui-logo-instructure-horizontal-full-color);
35	}
36	```
37	
38	## API
39	
40	- **`getLogoSvg(product, layout?, colorMode?)`** — the raw SVG (defaults: `horizontal`,
41	  `full-color`), or `undefined` if the combination doesn't exist.
42	- **`getLogoDataUri(product, layout?, colorMode?)`** — the logo as a base64 `data:image/svg+xml` URI.
43	- **`logosPlugin(options?)`** — the plugin. Its `css` hook contributes the `--instui-logo-*` image
44	  tokens. `options.position` is `"append"` (default) or `"prepend"`.
45	- **`logos`** — every logo's metadata (product, layout, color mode, name, path).
46	- **`products`** — the products that have logos.
47	- **`logosCss`** — the stylesheet text (the same as the `./logos.css` export).
48	- **`./logos.css`** — the ready image-token stylesheet, one `--instui-logo-<product>-<layout>-<mode>`
49	  custom property per logo.
50	
51	## License
52	
53	MIT — the plugin's code. The logos are Instructure trademarks; use them per Instructure's brand
54	guidelines.

1	# Plugins
2	
3	A pantoken plugin extends the token or CSS output without forking a package. You build one with
4	`definePlugin` from `@pantoken/plugin-kit`, then pass it to `buildTokens` or `toCss`.
5	
6	## Author a plugin
7	
8	Give `definePlugin` the hooks you implement. It returns a normal plugin, branded with the
9	capabilities inferred from those hooks. A plugin can extend the IR (`tokens`, `icons`), the CSS
10	output (`css`), or both.
11	
12	```ts
13	import { definePlugin } from "@pantoken/plugin-kit";
14	
15	export const brand = () =>
16	  definePlugin({
17	    name: "@acme/brand",
18	    tokens: (ctx) => [...ctx.tokens /* add records */],
19	    css: () => ({ append: ":root { /* … */ }" }),
20	  });
21	```
22	
23	## Capability-aware registration
24	
25	`buildTokens` and `toCss` run `checkPlugins` over the plugins you pass. It warns — it never throws —
26	when a plugin has no matching hook for the stage it's registered in, so a token-only plugin passed
27	to `toCss` is skipped with a note rather than silently doing nothing.
28	
29	## Compose plugins
30	
31	Build on top of another plugin with `extendPlugin`, or combine peers with `mergePlugin`:
32	
33	```ts
34	import { extendPlugin, mergePlugin } from "@pantoken/plugin-kit";
35	
36	const themed = extendPlugin(brand(), { css: () => ({ append: "/* extra */" }) });
37	const both = mergePlugin(brand(), icons());
38	```
39	
40	Same-stage hooks compose: `tokens` runs the base then the addition, `css` merges the two
41	contributions, and `icons` runs both.
42	
43	## Validate your plugin's output
44	
45	Run the shared drift checks from `@pantoken/utils` over your plugin's own output in its test, so a
46	typo or a renamed token fails fast and locally:
47	
48	```ts
49	import { danglingReferences, unknownReferences } from "@pantoken/utils";
50	import { tokens } from "@pantoken/tokens";
51	
52	// A self-contained contribution defines what it references, so nothing should dangle.
53	expect(danglingReferences(myPlugin().css!({ tokens, css: "" }).append ?? "")).toEqual([]);
54	
55	// A contribution that only references tokens defined elsewhere: every target must be a real token.
56	expect(unknownReferences(myBridgeCss, tokens)).toEqual([]);
57	```
58	
59	## The bundled plugins
60	
61	- `@pantoken/plugin-simple-icons` — brand icons from simple-icons, registered as icon tokens.
62	- `@pantoken/plugin-logos` — Instructure product logos as SVGs, data URIs, and `--instui-logo-*`
63	  image tokens.
64	- `@pantoken/plugin-prune-custom-props` — a PostCSS plugin (not a pantoken plugin) that drops
65	  unused custom properties from a stylesheet.
66	
67	A few things that used to be plugins now ship in `@pantoken/components`, since so many components need
68	them out of the box: elevation shadows (`--instui-elevation-*`, in `components.css`), the focus-outline
69	ring (in `base.css` — every focusable gets it when pantoken owns the page), and the Instructure brand
70	fonts (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next: `base.css` applies `--instui-font-family-base`; the opt-in
71	`@pantoken/components/fonts.css` loads the `@font-face` woff2s).
72	
73	See the [API reference](/api/) for each plugin's exports.

content.text:
Both sheets pass stylelint (including `cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`) and all plugin tests/checks. Done.

## What changed

The only tracked edits are the two generators — the CSS sheets and docs pages they produce are untracked build artifacts, regenerated by the docs build.

**[plugins/pantoken/stacking/scripts/generate.ts](plugins/pantoken/stacking/scripts/generate.ts)**
Emits a typed `@property` registration per token, pulling the concrete z-index from the `:root` block so defaults stay in lock-step:
```css
@property --instui-stacking-deepest { syntax: "<integer>"; inherits: true; initial-value: -9999; }
```
The docs CSS-API table now reads:

| Property | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--instui-stacking-deepest` | `<integer>` | `-9999` | The lowest stacking depth. |
| … | `<integer>` | `-1` / `1` / `9999` | … |

**[plugins/pantoken/logos/scripts/generate.ts](plugins/pantoken/logos/scripts/generate.ts)**
Emits a `@property` registration per logo — `syntax: "<url>"` (matching how the repo types data-URI tokens) with the logo's data URI as `initial-value`, encoded once and shared with the `:root` block. All 60 logo tokens now show `<url>` in Type and their data URI in Default.

## How it works

I traced the render path against the live cssdoc parser: the **Type** column comes from a `@property` at-rule's `syntax` (or a `<…>` on the `@cssproperty` line), and the **Default** column *only* populates from a `@property` at-rule's `initial-value` — prose defaults and `:root` values don't reach it. The `@cssproperty` doc lines keep supplying the descriptions; cssdoc merges the two.

## Cost to flag (as discussed)

The logos at-rules duplicate each ~5 KB base64 blob, so:
- `logos.css` grew **289 KB → 575 KB** (this ships via `./logos.css`, since `pack.entry.logos` builds from the generated sheet).
- `docs/api/css/logos.md` is now ~286 KB — its Default column holds 60 full data URIs, so it's not human-readable. Stacking stays clean.

The runtime plugin output (`LOGOS_CSS` / the `css` hook) is unchanged — the registrations live only in the static generated sheet, matching how stacking already scopes its doc block.

Verified: `vp test` and `vp check` pass for both plugins, stylelint (incl. `cssdoc/valid-doc-comments`) reports zero warnings on both sheets, and the CSS-API build regenerated all 66 pages with the populated tables. Nothing is committed.
